findings.failure_scenario: A multithreaded app (e.g., LangChain callbacks in a thread pool) creates its first RunTrees concurrently: both threads read _CLIENT is None and both run Client(), each starting its own background _tracing_control_thread_func thread (auto_batch_tracing defaults to True) and HTTP session; the second assignment wins _CLIENT while the first thread's RunTree keeps using its own orphaned client, leaving two tracing batch threads and two sessions alive for the process lifetime with divergent configuration (e.g., a caller passing timeout_ms=(20_000, 90_001) gets a different instance than the process-wide cache).
findings.summary: Removing the _LOCK from get_cached_client reintroduces a race where concurrent first calls each construct a separate Client, and one caller keeps an instance that is not the cached one

findings.failure_scenario: A contributor (or agent) follows AGENTS.md and runs 'make test' from python/ (as instructed at lines 10, 18, and 25): make errors with 'No rule to make target test' because the Makefile has only 'tests:' (line 26), no 'test' target, no pattern rules, and no includes. The documented pre-PR checklist is unusable.
findings.summary: AGENTS.md now instructs running 'make test', but python/Makefile only defines a 'tests' target, so the documented command fails for every contributor

findings.failure_scenario: The test suite is run from a source tarball or copied checkout (no .git work tree), a repo with no origin remote, or a remote URL that doesn't contain 'langsmith-sdk': get_git_info() returns a dict with commit or remote_url None, so assert git_info["commit"] is not None or the 'langsmith-sdk' membership check raises AssertionError and the suite fails — the exact cases the removed try/except+pytest.skip existed to tolerate.
findings.summary: Deleting the pytest.skip fallback makes test_git_info hard-fail in any environment without git metadata, breaking the suite where it previously skipped

findings.failure_scenario: Non-behavioral maintainability defect: after the with _LOCK wrapper was deleted, the leftover double-checked-locking idiom has no effect — any reader may assume the nested check provides synchronization or serves a purpose, when it is simply redundant and should be collapsed into the single outer check.
findings.summary: The inner 'if _CLIENT is None:' is now dead code: with the lock removed it re-checks the same global the outer if just evaluated and can never be False, so it guards nothing
